observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly converts quoted property names containing Unicode escape sequences into unquoted property names, resulting in invalid JavaScript output when those characters are not valid in identifiers.
reasoning_summary: The bug is caused by a failure to validate whether a property name containing a Unicode escape sequence is a valid identifier before deciding to remove the quotes. This is a classic missing guard/validation check (Checking) where the compiler assumes all property names can be converted to dotted notation without verifying the character constraints of the property name.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the conversion logic is flawed, the root cause is the missing check for identifier validity before applying the conversion algorithm.
